_note: Composition A — editorial/magazine led. Full-bleed plated-course hero, alternating menu-section rows that read like a printed cookbook, photo-led closing CTA.

data.title: A dinner house grown within thirty miles of the table
data.subtitle: Five-course tasting menus built from the day's harvest at three Driftless farms we know by name. Service begins at 5:30 and 7:30; reservations open four weeks ahead.

data.heading: The week's menu
data.intro: Menus turn weekly to follow what's coming out of the ground. Each course is paired with a wine drawn from our cellar of small-production Wisconsin and upper-Midwest producers.

items.title: First — Garden
items.description: Late-summer tomatoes from Ridge Farm with smoked ricotta, marigold honey, and sourdough hearth-bread. Eat with your hands.
bullets: Paired with a 2023 Wisconsin orange wine, La Crosse blend

items.title: Second — From the river
items.description: Slow-poached brook trout from a spring-fed pond two valleys over, finished with brown butter, sorrel, and trout roe.
bullets: Paired with a 2022 Minnesota Marquette, light pour

items.title: Third — From the field
items.description: Pasture-raised lamb shoulder, slow-cooked on the wood hearth with juniper, root vegetables glazed in lamb fat, and a pomegranate-port reduction.
bullets: Paired with a 2021 Iowa Frontenac Noir reserve

items.title: Fourth — Sweet
items.description: Roasted plums from the Mineral Point Orchard, brown butter financier, and a small glass of late-harvest Edelweiss. Coffee is roasted three blocks away.
bullets: Coffee from Working Draft, Madison · Tea by request

data.heading: Reserve your table
data.subtitle: Two seatings each evening, Tuesday through Saturday. Reservations open four weeks ahead and tend to fill within a few days — joining the standby list often gets you in.
bullets: Vegetarian and shellfish-free menus by request, 48 hours ahead
Private dining room seats up to 10; weekday lunches by arrangement
Walk-ins seated at the chef's counter when space allows
